Memory can be explained as a clock. The second hand is working memory, the minute hand is short term memory and the hour hand is long term memory.
The second hand is constantly moving and demands constant energy. It only focuses on something for a short period of time and then moves on to the next thing. It is by far the most active.
The minute hand moves much slower and holds onto information for longer. It takes the key things from the second hand and stores them into chunks which can be referred back to in the future. If the information is not engaged with often enough it can be easily lost as the hand moves to the next number on the clock face
Finally the hour hand moves extremely slowly. It tracks the big picture capturing the important events and the long term picture of time passing in life
